mainTopic: Counting a רגל toward mourning, how much mourning before a רגל is needed, and the one-day rule for late news of a death
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge against רבא, who held that the רגל does not count toward the שלשים when the burial was during the רגל. A first ברייתא can be read so that it does not contradict him. A second ברייתא clearly speaks of a burial during the רגל and still counts the רגל, so רבא is refuted, and רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר rule the same way. Next, a ברייתא asks how much mourning before a רגל is needed so that the רגל cancels the rest of שבעה: three days or even one hour. רבי יוחנן says even one hour and רבא says three days. In practice, רבינא rules that even one hour is enough. The גמרא then learns the seven days of mourning from the פסוק 'I will turn your festivals into mourning,' and uses the one-day עצרת for late news of a death (שמועה רחוקה). The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא that late news gets only one day, because in mourning we follow the lenient view, and רבא applies this even to a parent. A story about רבי חייא then begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The general rule: mourning practices pause for the Festival, public comforting does not
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its clause about burial during the רגל and gives a general rule. Practices of אבל are put on hold by the רגל. Public visits to comfort the mourner are not put on hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...because people already came to comfort him during the Festival. The general rule is this: anything done because of mourning is interrupted by the Festival. Anything done because of the public's involvement with the mourner is not interrupted by the Festival.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא being quoted against רבא. It finishes one line and then states a general rule about what the רגל interrupts and what it does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Personal mourning practices like not working are not kept on the רגל, so they start only after it ends. Comforting the mourner is different, because people really do come to comfort him during the רגל. That is why the visits already made during the רגל still count afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter
Mourning, or a mourner
A Festival (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)
Interrupts it, puts it on hold
The public's involvement, people coming to comfort the mourner

steps.confusionAlert: 'The רגל interrupts it' does not mean the mourning practice is cancelled. It is only put on hold during the רגל and starts or continues afterward.

phrases.english: for they already occupied themselves with him during the Festival.
phrases.notes: This is the tail end of a line from the ברייתא that started before this section, about someone who buried his relative during the רגל.

phrases.english: The general principle of the matter:
Anything that is because of mourning —
the Festival interrupts it.
And anything that is because of the public's involvement —
phrases.notes: He means people coming to visit and comfort the mourner.

phrases.english: the Festival does not interrupt it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא quoted before this section as a challenge to רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mourning practices are put on hold by the רגל. Public comforting is not put on hold.

steps.title: Burial three days before the end of the Festival
steps.stepSummary: If the burial was three days before the רגל ended, the mourner counts שבעה after the רגל. The public visits him only on the first four days, because they already visited during the רגל. The ברייתא ends: 'and the רגל counts for him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he buried his relative three days before the end of the Festival, he counts seven days after the Festival. On the first four days, people come to comfort him. On the last three days, they do not need to come, because they already came during the Festival. And the Festival counts for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its last case, a burial during the רגל, and closes with the key words 'the רגל counts for him.' Those closing words are what the גמרא will argue about next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This applies the general rule from step 1. His own mourning starts only after the רגל, so he counts a full שבעה then. The three days of comforting during the רגל still count, so people only need to come for four more days. The closing line says the רגל counts toward the שלשים, which seems to go against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The seven-day mourning period
Occupy themselves with him, come to comfort him
Counts for him toward the mourning period

phrases.english: If he buried him three days at the end of the Festival —
phrases.notes: Meaning the burial happened during the רגל, with three days of it still left.

phrases.english: he counts seven after the Festival;
the first four days —
the public occupies itself with him;
the last three days —
the public does not occupy itself with him,
for they already occupied themselves [with him] during the Festival,
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording, but the meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: and the Festival counts for him.
phrases.notes: Counts toward the thirty-day mourning period. This is the line the next step argues about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the general rule to a burial near the end of the רגל and closes the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When burial is three days before the רגל ends, the mourner counts שבעה afterward and needs comforting only on the first four days. The ברייתא ends 'the רגל counts for him.'

steps.title: Doesn't 'the Festival counts' refer to the burial during the Festival?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'the רגל counts for him' goes on the סיפא, the case of burial during the רגל. If so, the ברייתא directly contradicts רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the line 'and the Festival counts for him' talking about the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the ברייתא into a challenge. It argues that 'the רגל counts' belongs to the last case, a burial during the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא held that if the burial was during the רגל, the רגל does not count toward the שלשים. If 'the רגל counts' refers to the סיפא, the ברייתא says the opposite in exactly רבא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? (introduces a suggested reading that leads to a challenge)
The later or last clause of a source

phrases.english: What, is it not on the latter clause!
phrases.notes: The latter clause is the case just read in step 2, where the burial happened during the רגל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the closing line of the ברייתא to challenge רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the רגל does not count toward שלשים when the burial was during the רגל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'the רגל counts' goes on the case of burial during the רגל, the ברייתא directly says the opposite of רבא.

steps.title: No, it refers to the burial before the Festival
steps.stepSummary: רבא's side answers that 'the רגל counts' goes on the רישא, the earlier case of burial before the רגל. In that case mourning had already started, so of course the רגל counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is talking about the first case.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is pushed off. The line 'the רגל counts' is read as going on the first case, not the last one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the burial was before the רגל, so mourning had already begun. רבא agrees the רגל counts toward שלשים in that case. The ברייתא no longer proves anything about a burial during the רגל.

keyTerms.meaning: The first or earlier clause of a source

phrases.english: No, on the first clause.
phrases.notes: The first clause was quoted before this section and dealt with a burial before the רגל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by moving the key line to a different clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading which clause a line refers to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'The רגל counts' refers to the burial during the רגל, which would contradict רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'The רגל counts' refers to the burial before the רגל, which רבא agrees with.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: buried at the start of the Festival, and the Festival still counts
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא is brought against רבא. It explicitly describes a burial at the beginning of the רגל and still says the רגל counts toward שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: 'The Festival counts toward the thirty days. How so? If he buried his relative at the beginning of the Festival, he counts seven days after the Festival. His work is done by others, and his servants work privately inside his house. People do not need to come comfort him, because they already came during the Festival. And the Festival counts for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is raised from a different ברייתא. This time the case is clearly a burial during the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא opens by saying the רגל counts for the שלשים and then gives only one example, a burial at the start of the רגל. There is no earlier clause to move the line to, so the answer from step 4 cannot work here. It directly contradicts רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him (with a source)
The thirty-day mourning period
How so? (introduces an explanation)
Privately, out of public view

steps.whyThisMatters: The challenge works because this ברייתא's wording is clear. The earlier one could be read two ways, but this one cannot.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: רֶגֶל עוֹלֶה לוֹ לְמִנְיַן שְׁלֹשִׁים,
phrases.english: He challenged him: A Festival counts for him toward the count of thirty,
phrases.notes: The challenge is aimed at רבא.

phrases.english: How so? If he buried him at the beginning of the Festival —
he counts seven after the Festival,
and his work is done by others,
and his menservants and maidservants work
in private inside his house,
and the public does not occupy itself with him,
for they already occupied themselves with him during the Festival,
and the Festival counts for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a stronger source is brought that cannot be explained the same way.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that the רגל does not count toward שלשים when the burial was during the רגל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא clearly discusses only a burial at the start of the רגל and says the רגל counts, so there is no other clause to move the line to.

steps.title: רבא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes with תיובתא: רבא's view is refuted. The רגל counts toward שלשים even when the burial was during the רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא declares that the second ברייתא disproves רבא, and no answer is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the second ברייתא is clear and cannot be re-read, רבא's position falls. The result is that a burial during the רגל still lets the רגל count toward the שלשים.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; the view is disproved

steps.whatToRemember: Practices of אבל are put on hold during the רגל, but public comforting continues. The first ברייתא could be read so that it does not contradict רבא. The second ברייתא, about a burial at the start of the רגל, clearly says the רגל counts toward שלשים, so רבא is refuted.

phrases.english: A refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 5 with a final refutation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבא is refuted. The רגל counts toward שלשים even when the burial took place during the רגל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר rule that the festival counts even for a burial during it
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן rules the רגל counts toward שלשים even if the burial was during the רגל. רבי אלעזר also gave this ruling to his son רבי פדת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he reported that רבי יוחנן said: even if someone buried his relative during the רגל, the רגל still counts. רבי אלעזר also told his son רבי פדת the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: After רבא was refuted, the גמרא brings two great אמוראים who rule the same way as the conclusion: the רגל counts toward שלשים even when the burial was during the רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 ended with the ברייתא refuting רבא. Now we learn that this is also the practical ruling of רבי יוחנן and רבי אלעזר, so the conclusion is not just a refutation but the actual הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל, bringing a teaching)
He buried him during the festival
Ruled / gave a practical ruling
The thirty-day mourning period

steps.whatToRemember: The final rule: the רגל counts toward שלשים even when the burial took place during the רגל.

phrases.english: When Ravin came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even if he buried him during the Festival,
phrases.notes: The rest of the thought is left unsaid: even then, the רגל counts toward the thirty days.

phrases.english: And so Rabbi Elazar ruled
for Rabbi Pedat, his son:
Even if he buried him during the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֲפִילּוּ קְבָרוֹ בָּרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the conclusion of step 6 with practical rulings from אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The רגל counts toward שלשים even if the burial was during the רגל.

steps.title: How long before the festival must the bed be overturned
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבי אליעזר says three days of overturning the bed before the רגל are needed so the mourner does not have to resume after it. חכמים say even one day or one hour is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a mourner kept his bed turned over for three days before the רגל, he does not need to turn it over again after the רגל. This is רבי אליעזר's view. חכמים say that even one day, or even one hour, is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ברייתא. The question is how much mourning before a רגל is needed so that the רגל cancels the rest of שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning over the bed (כפיית המטה) is one of the practices of שבעה, and here it stands for keeping שבעה before the רגל. Both sides agree that some mourning before the רגל lets the רגל cancel the rest. They only argue about the minimum: three days, or even a single hour.

keyTerms.meaning: Overturning the bed, one of the mourning practices
He fulfilled / observed
The תנא who requires three days
The majority of the Sages, who say even one hour

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי אליעזר (the תנא in this ברייתא) with רבי אלעזר (the אמורא in the previous step). The names look almost the same.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
If he fulfilled the overturning of the bed
for three days before the Festival,
he does not need to overturn it after the Festival,
these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד, אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: Even one day, even one hour.
phrases.notes: The Sages mean that even this little bit of mourning before the רגל is enough, so he does not need to resume after it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קִיֵּים כְּפִיַּית הַמִּטָּה שְׁלֹשָׁה יָמִים קוֹדֶם הָרֶגֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the minimum mourning before a רגל needed to cancel שבעה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: three days before the רגל cancels the rest. חכמים: even one day or one hour.

steps.title: The dispute goes back to בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון explains that this argument already existed between בית שמאי, who said three days, and בית הלל, who said even one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון said: these are really the views of בית שמאי and בית הלל. בית שמאי say three days, and בית הלל say even one day.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא tells us where the ברייתא's dispute comes from. רבי אליעזר's view matches בית שמאי, and חכמים's view matches בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Linking רבי אליעזר to בית שמאי and חכמים to בית הלל raises the stakes. Normally we follow בית הלל, which would seem to favor 'even one day.' This sets up the rulings in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: These are exactly the words of (this view is really that earlier view)
The school of שמאי
The school of הלל
רבי אלעזר, son of רבי שמעון בר יוחאי

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon said:
These are exactly the words of Beit Shammai,
phrases.notes: He means רבי אליעזר's view (three days) is really בית שמאי's view.

phrases.english: and these are exactly the words of Beit Hillel.
For Beit Shammai say: Three days,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: Even one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: הֵן הֵן דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Traces the ברייתא's dispute back to בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר follows בית שמאי (three days), and חכמים follow בית הלל (even one day).

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules even one day or one hour
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules like חכמים: even one day, even one hour, of mourning before the רגל is enough. The chain of transmission is reported in two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said in the name of רבי חייא בר אבא, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן (or, in another version, רבי יוחנן told this directly to both of them): even one day, even one hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's ruling, which follows חכמים (and בית הלל). It also notes two versions of who heard it from whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two versions only disagree about how the teaching was passed down, not about what it says. Either way, רבי יוחנן holds that even a short time of mourning before the רגל cancels the rest of שבעה.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say it (another version of the report)
An אמורא, one of the people who passed on רבי יוחנן's ruling
A student of רבי יוחנן

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rav Huna said that Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said,
and some say it this way:

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said to Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba
and to Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד, אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: Even one day, even one hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an אמורא's ruling on the dispute, siding with חכמים and בית הלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even one day, or even one hour, of mourning before the רגל is enough.

steps.title: רבא rules like our תנא, who requires three days
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רבי יוחנן. He rules that the הלכה follows 'our תנא,' the תנא of our משנה, who requires three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the הלכה follows our תנא, who said three days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the opposite ruling. Three days of mourning before the רגל are needed to cancel the rest of שבעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Our תנא' is the תנא of our משנה, which spoke of burying three days before the רגל. רבא gives weight to the anonymous משנה, even though the three-day view matches בית שמאי. So two אמוראים end up ruling in opposite directions.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows
Our תנא (the one who taught our משנה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says even one hour before the רגל is enough. רבא says the הלכה follows our משנה: three days.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the same topic as the תיובתא against רבא in step 6. That was about שלשים. This ruling is about how much of שבעה must be kept before the רגל.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The halacha follows our Tanna
phrases.notes: This is the תנא of our משנה, which spoke about burying three days before the רגל.

phrases.english: who said three.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הֲלָכָה כְּתַנָּא דִּידַן דְּאָמַר שְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 10 and rules like the three-day view.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבא, a mourner must keep at least three days of שבעה before the רגל for the רגל to cancel the rest of שבעה.

steps.title: רב חביבא asks רבינא what the practical ruling is
steps.stepSummary: While רבינא is visiting סורא on the Euphrates, רב חביבא asks him what the הלכה is about mourning before a רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא came to סורא on the Euphrates. רב חביבא asked him: What is the הלכה?
steps.whatsHappening: After hearing two opposite rulings, the גמרא now sets up a practical question. רב חביבא asks רבינא which ruling we actually follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ruled that even one day or one hour of mourning before the רגל is enough. רבא ruled like the תנא of our משנה, who requires three days. רב חביבא wants to know which view is the final practical ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come / visited
What is the practical ruling?
סורא on the Euphrates River

phrases.english: Ravina happened to come to Sura on the Euphrates.
Rav Chaviva said to Ravina:
What is the halacha?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical ruling after רבי יוחנן (step 10) and רבא (step 11) disagreed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the practical הלכה follows רבי יוחנן (one day or one hour) or רבא (three days).

steps.title: רבינא rules that even one day or one hour is enough
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that even one day, and even one hour, of mourning before the רגל is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even one day, and even one hour.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives the practical answer. A short amount of mourning before the רגל is enough, as רבי יוחנן ruled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא's answer repeats the exact words of חכמים and רבי יוחנן. So in practice the הלכה does not follow רבא's ruling of three days. Even one hour of mourning before the רגל means the רגל cancels the rest of the שבעה.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
One hour (a short time)

steps.whatToRemember: In practice, even one day or even one hour of mourning before a רגל is enough. This follows רבי יוחנן and חכמים, not רבא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the practical הלכה for a mourner whose relative died shortly before a רגל.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד, וַאֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת.
phrases.english: Even one day, and even one hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲפִילּוּ יוֹם אֶחָד, וַאֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חביבא's question from step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה is that even one day or one hour of mourning before the רגל is enough.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The practical ruling follows רבי יוחנן and חכמים against רבא.

steps.title: The source for seven days of mourning
steps.stepSummary: Three אמוראים sitting together derive the seven days of אבילות from the פסוק 'And I will turn your festivals into mourning'. A חג lasts seven days, so mourning lasts seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא, רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא were sitting in the pavilion of רבי יצחק בן אלעזר. A teaching came out of their discussion. From where do we know that mourning lasts seven days? From the פסוק 'And I will turn your festivals into mourning.' Just as a festival lasts seven days, mourning also lasts seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: where the Torah source is for the seven days of mourning. A group of אמוראים learns it from a פסוק that links חג and mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares festivals to mourning. The festivals of פסח and סוכות last seven days, so mourning is also seven days.

keyTerms.meaning: Pavilion or tent-like room
A teaching came out of their discussion
From where do we know?
Mourning
Festival

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba was sitting,
and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha,
in the pavilion of Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar.
A teaching came out from among them:
From where do we know that mourning is seven days?
As it is written: 'And I will turn your festivals into mourning.'
phrases.notes: עמוס 8:10

phrases.english: Just as a festival is seven days,
so too mourning is seven days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the source for seven days of mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seven days of אבילות are learned from the comparison of mourning to a seven-day חג.

steps.title: Why not compare mourning to the one-day עצרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof. עצרת is also a חג, and it lasts only one day, so maybe mourning should be one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that it is like עצרת, which is only one day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from step 14. The word 'festivals' could also point to עצרת, which is only one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on a חג being seven days. But not every חג is seven days, since עצרת is one day. So the פסוק could just as easily teach one day of mourning.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead...
שבועות
One day

phrases.english: But say it is like Shavuot,
phrases.notes: עצרת is the name the חכמים use for שבועות.

phrases.english: which is one day!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the derivation of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that mourning is seven days because a חג is seven days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עצרת is also a חג but lasts only one day, so the comparison could teach one day of mourning instead of seven.

steps.title: The one-day comparison is used for late news of a death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the comparison to the one-day עצרת is already needed for ריש לקיש's teaching. When someone hears late news of a death (שמועה רחוקה), he mourns only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: That comparison is needed for the teaching of ריש לקיש. ריש לקיש said in the name of רבי יהודה נשיאה: From where do we know that late news of a death is mourned for only one day? As it is written: 'And I will turn your festivals into mourning,' and we find that עצרת, which is one day, is called a festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The one-day side of the comparison is not lost. It is used for a different case, late news of a death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק teaches two things. The seven-day festivals teach the normal seven days of mourning. The one-day עצרת teaches that שמועה רחוקה is mourned for only one day. So both lengths are used, and each fits a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for something else
Late news of a relative's death
We find
Is called

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying עצרת is not a חג. It agrees עצרת is called a חג. It just uses that one-day comparison for the special case of late news, not for regular mourning.

phrases.english: That is needed
for what Reish Lakish taught.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה:
phrases.english: As Reish Lakish said in the name of Rabbi Yehuda Nesia:
From where do we know that late news of a death
is mourned for only one day?
As it is written: 'And I will turn your festivals into mourning.'
And we find that Shavuot,
which is one day, is called a festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the competing reading to a different teaching (מיבעי ליה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since עצרת is one day, the פסוק might teach that all mourning is one day.
steps.terutzMaskana: The one-day comparison teaches the law of שמועה רחוקה, so regular mourning stays seven days.

steps.title: Recent news versus late news: רבי עקיבא's view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that שמועה קרובה requires שבעה and שלשים, while שמועה רחוקה requires only one day. רבי עקיבא defines news that comes within thirty days as recent, and news after thirty days as late.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Recent news of a death is mourned with seven days and thirty days. Late news is mourned for only one day. What counts as recent and what counts as late? Recent means within thirty days. Late means after thirty days. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that spells out the law of recent and late news. It also defines the dividing line, according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא matches ריש לקיש's teaching that late news gets only one day. It adds the exact line: thirty days from the death. News inside that window gets full שבעה and שלשים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Recent news of a death
Applies / is observed
The thirty-day mourning period

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Recent news of a death
is mourned with seven days and thirty days.
Late news
is mourned for only one day.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיזוֹ הִיא קְרוֹבָה וְאֵיזוֹ הִיא רְחוֹקָה?
phrases.english: What counts as recent, and what counts as late?
Recent is within thirty days,
phrases.notes: Thirty days counted from the death, not from when he hears the news.

phrases.english: late is after thirty days.
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that fits ריש לקיש's teaching about שמועה רחוקה and defines its terms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, news arriving within thirty days requires שבעה and שלשים, and news arriving after thirty days requires only one day.

steps.title: The Sages say all news requires full mourning
steps.stepSummary: חכמים disagree with רבי עקיבא. Both recent and late news require שבעה and שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: Both recent news and late news are mourned with seven days and thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the opposing view. חכמים do not accept a one-day rule for late news.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, the timing of the news makes no difference. Whenever a person hears of a relative's death, he keeps the full שבעה and שלשים. This disagrees with רבי עקיבא and with ריש לקיש's one-day teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority view)
Both this and that

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: news after thirty days requires only one day of mourning. חכמים: all news requires full שבעה and שלשים.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Both recent news
and late news
are mourned with seven days and thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אַחַת שְׁמוּעָה קְרוֹבָה וְאַחַת שְׁמוּעָה רְחוֹקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, both recent and late news require full שבעה and שלשים.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא because in mourning we follow the lenient view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that usually the majority wins over one lenient opinion, but here the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא, based on שמואל's rule that in אבילות we follow the lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Usually, when one person is lenient and many are strict, the הלכה follows the many. This case is an exception. Even though רבי עקיבא is lenient and the חכמים are strict, the הלכה follows רבי עקיבא. That is because שמואל said: in mourning, the הלכה follows the lenient view.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the argument from the last two steps between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים. The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא: late news needs only one day of mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal rule is that the majority wins, so we would expect the חכמים to win. רבי יוחנן says this case is an exception. שמואל's rule explains why: in mourning laws, the lenient view wins.

keyTerms.meaning: A single sage holding a view alone
The many, the majority of sages
Being lenient
Being strict
In mourning, the הלכה follows the lenient view

steps.whatToRemember: Practical הלכה: late news (after thirty days) needs only one day of mourning, like רבי עקיבא, because in mourning we follow the lenient view.
steps.whyThisMatters: שמואל's rule is a general rule for all mourning laws, not just this one case.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Wherever you find
one person being lenient and many being strict,
the halacha follows the many.
Except for this one,
phrases.notes: "This one" is the argument we just saw about late news of a death.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מֵקֵיל
phrases.english: where even though Rabbi Akiva is lenient
and the Sages are strict,
the halacha follows Rabbi Akiva.
As Shmuel said:
The halacha follows the words of the lenient one in mourning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the argument between רבי עקיבא and the חכמים from steps 17-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי עקיבא: late news needs only one day of mourning, because in mourning we follow the lenient view.

steps.title: רב חסדא rules one day for late news of a father's death
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא got late news of his father's death, and רב חסדא told him late news needs only one day of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: News of his father's death reached רב חנינא from בי חוזאי. He came to רב חסדא, who told him: late news needs only one day of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story showing the ruling from the last step put into practice, even for a father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death was the father's, the closest kind of relative. Still, רב חסדא gave only one day. So the leniency for late news applies to parents too.

keyTerms.meaning: Late news of a death, arriving after thirty days
A faraway region; news from there arrived late
Applies for only one day

phrases.english: To Rav Chanina there came
news about his father from Bei Chozai.
phrases.notes: The news came from far away and reached him late. That is why the ruling is about late news.

phrases.english: He came before Rav Chisda.
He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמוּעָה רְחוֹקָה אֵינָהּ נוֹהֶגֶת אֶלָּא יוֹם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Late news applies for only one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חֲנִינָא אַתְיָא לֵיהּ שְׁמוּעָה דַאֲבוּהּ מִבֵּי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical case following the ruling in step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even for a father, late news needs only one day of mourning.

steps.title: רבא rules one day for late news of a mother's death
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אמי got late news of his mother's death, and רבא told him late news needs only one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: News of his mother's death reached רב נתן בר אמי from בי חוזאי. He came to רבא, who told him: the sages have said that late news needs only one day of mourning.
steps.whatsHappening: A second story with the same ruling, this time for a mother. It also sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gives the same ruling as רב חסדא, now for a mother. The word בלבד ("only") stresses that one day is all that is needed. This sets up רב נתן's objection.

keyTerms.meaning: "They have said": quoting an accepted teaching
Only, alone

phrases.aramaic: רַב נָתָן בַּר אַמֵּי אֲתָא לֵיהּ
phrases.english: To Rav Natan bar Ami there came
news about his mother from Bei Chozai.
He came before Rava.
He said to him: They have said,
late news applies
for only one day alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נָתָן בַּר אַמֵּי אֲתָא לֵיהּ שְׁמוּעָה דְּאִימֵּיהּ מִבֵּי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story to step 20, with a mother instead of a father.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even for a mother, late news needs only one day of mourning.

steps.title: A ברייתא says parents need full mourning even with late news
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן challenges רבא with a ברייתא: the one-day rule is only for the other relatives, but for a father or mother one keeps שבעה and שלשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן challenged רבא from a ברייתא: When is the one-day rule said? For the five other relatives one must mourn. But for one's father and mother, one keeps שבעה and שלשים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נתן challenges רבא's ruling, using a ברייתא that treats parents differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gave one day for a mother. The ברייתא limits the one-day leniency to the other relatives. For parents, even late news needs the full שבעה and שלשים, so רבא's ruling seems to go against the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a source
"In what case are these words said?": limiting a rule
Relatives one is obligated to mourn
The seven-day and thirty-day mourning periods

phrases.english: He challenged him:
In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: "These words" are the rule that late news needs only one day.

phrases.english: For the five relatives one must mourn,
phrases.notes: These are the close relatives you must mourn other than your parents, like a child, a sibling or a spouse.

phrases.english: but for his father and for his mother
seven and thirty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's ruling in step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling of one day for late news of a mother's death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the one-day rule does not apply to parents, who always need שבעה and שלשים.

steps.title: רבא says the ברייתא is only one view, and we do not follow it
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא holds a view of individual sages, and the halacha does not follow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: That is the view of individuals, and we do not hold like it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. He does not explain the ברייתא away. He simply says we do not follow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא accepts that the ברייתא really does make parents an exception. He calls it a minority view (יחידאה) that we do not follow, so his ruling stands. The next step shows which individuals held that strict view.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the view of individuals
We do not hold like it

phrases.english: He said to him: It is an individual view,
and we do not hold like it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יְחִידָאָה הִיא, וְלָא סְבִירָא לַן כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejecting the source as a minority opinion that is not followed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is the accepted halacha, so parents need שבעה and שלשים even with late news.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is a minority view. The halacha is one day even for parents.

steps.title: Stories showing that the strict view came from specific individuals
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא with two stories. In one, אלישע בן אבויה and the elders with him told רבי צדוק to keep full mourning three years after his father died. In the other, רבי אחייה kept full mourning for his son who died far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי צדוק's father died in גינזק, and he was told three years later. He asked אלישע בן אבויה and the elders with him, and they said: keep שבעה and שלשים. And when רבי אחייה's son died in the diaspora, he sat שבעה and שלשים for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his answer by showing which sages actually held the strict view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The strict practice shows up in rulings and actions of specific people: אלישע בן אבויה and his group, and רבי אחייה. This supports רבא's claim that the strict view belongs to individuals. The halacha follows the lenient view instead.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
A story about something that happened
Keep, observe
The diaspora, outside ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: These stories seem to support the strict view! But רבא uses them only to show who held that view: a few individuals. We do not follow them.
steps.whatToRemember: The halacha: late news of a death needs only one day of mourning, even for a father or mother. The strict view belongs to individuals and is not followed.

phrases.english: As it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵת אָבִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי צָדוֹק בְּגִינְזַק,
phrases.english: It once happened that the father of Rabbi Tzadok died in Ginzak,
and they told him after three years.

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא וְשָׁאַל אֶת אֱלִישָׁע בֶּן אֲבוּיָה
phrases.english: He came and asked Elisha ben Avuya
and the elders with him, and they said:
Keep seven and thirty.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁמֵּת בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֲחִיָּיה בַּגּוֹלָה,
phrases.english: And when the son of Rabbi Achiyya died in the diaspora,
he sat for him seven and thirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מַעֲשֶׂה וּמֵת אָבִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי צָדוֹק בְּגִינְזַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's claim in step 23 that the strict view is held by individuals.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the strict view for parents is only a minority view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with two stories: אלישע בן אבויה's ruling for רבי צדוק, and רבי אחייה's own practice.

steps.title: Is that really so? The story of רב and רבי חייא begins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the view just quoted in רבא's ברייתא. It opens a story: רב, who was both the brother's son and the sister's son of רבי חייא, went up to ארץ ישראל, and רבי חייא asked him, 'Is your father alive?'
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב, the son of רבי חייא's brother, who was also the son of רבי חייא's sister, went up there. רבי חייא asked him: Is Father alive?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the view of רבי אחייה from the last step by starting a story about רב and his uncle רבי חייא. This line only sets up the story. The point of the challenge comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אִינִי tells us the גמרא doubts that the view in רבא's ברייתא really holds. It brings in a real-life case about late news of a death in רבי חייא's own family, so we can see how mourning was actually kept. It also tells us that רב was related to רבי חייא through both his father and his mother. That is why news about either parent would matter to רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is that so?" A word that opens a challenge to what was just said
"But surely..." It brings in a source or story that seems to contradict what was said
Son of his brother (nephew through the father's side)
Son of his sister (nephew through the mother's side)
Went up there, meaning to ארץ ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the challenge to be finished here. This line only opens the story. How רבי חייא mourned, which is the actual point, comes in the continuation.

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב, בַּר אֲחוּהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא
phrases.english: But Rav, the son of Rabbi Chiya's brother,
who was also the son of Rabbi Chiya's sister,
when he went up there,
phrases.notes: "There" means ארץ ישראל, where רבי חייא lived.

phrases.english: he (Rabbi Chiya) said to him: Is Father alive?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the view of רבי אחייה that רבא's ברייתא brought in Step 24, using a story about רבי חייא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 24's ברייתא that רבי אחייה himself kept שבעה and שלשים after late news of a death.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story about how רבי חייא himself mourned after late news of a family death will show a practice that seems to go against that view. The story starts here and is finished in the next lines.
